hunts.label: Saturday, Nov 14
hunts.subtitle: Frost on the leaves, sun on the trunks by seven. Sit high, face the light's far side, and let the squirrels come out to warm up.

rules.title: Rules for this hunt
items: No clock change before this hunt. The next one is Sunday Mar 14, 2027 (spring forward).
**Frost advisory until 8 am.** Dress warm and expect loud, crunchy leaves until the sun melts the frost.
**Bear season opens today** (Nov 14 to 22). You do not hunt bear, but other hunters may be out. Deer gun season is still open for them: stay in orange.
**Saturday is a crow day** (Wed, Fri, Sat only). Dove segment 2 and snipe are open. Quail opens next Saturday, Nov 21.
Woodcock is closed until Dec 10.
rules.note: Small game focus for the rest of the season. Deer: tag filled. Do not shoot a deer.

items: Walk-in: about **34F** with frost. Friday night low is forecast near 34.
9 am: mid-40s (assumption). The afternoon high is near **55F**.
Wind: **north 3 to 6 mph** overnight, then **northwest 5 to 11 mph** Saturday. No gust figure was listed.
Sky: partly cloudy overnight, then **sunny**. Widespread frost before 8 am. No rain mentioned.
Sunrise **6:43 am**. Legal light **6:13 am**.
Moon: **waxing crescent, about 25 percent**. Moonrise is near 11:40 am, so the morning is dark and moonless.
conditions.meaning: Assumption: frost and a clear sky keep squirrels in the nest until the sun reaches the trunks, then they feed hard. Expect the best squirrel and rabbit movement from about 7:15 to 9:00, as the frost melts and the breeze picks up from the northwest.
conditions.hours_note: No hour-by-hour table was available for the hunt morning, so the hourly chart is left out. Temperatures above come from the daily forecast and are estimates.

wind.label: NW 5 to 11, lighter and more northerly before dawn (assumption)

in_season.tip: Feed trees on sunlit trunks after 7:15.
Sunny edges of thick cover and the feed bins area, after the frost melts.
Last ones heading to dens at first light.
Opportunity from the seat. Shots north only.

Open, but skipped today. Ducks need steel shot, HIP, federal stamp, and state waterfowl privilege.

in_season: Quail opens Nov 21. Woodcock opens Dec 10.
Deer: tag filled for the season. Do not shoot a deer.
Bear and bobcat are open. You do not hunt them. Stay aware near the swamp.

plan.title: Center Loop Rise
plan.why: The sun comes up in the southeast, so sit with it behind you and face **northwest**. The trunks in front of you light up first, and squirrels coming out to warm up are easy to see. Pick the gentle rise at the center of the loop trail, where oaks, hickories, and holly stand within 40 yards to the NW. Sit against a wide pine trunk on the south side of that rise. The NW breeze is in your face, so your scent drifts behind you, away from the squirrels. Frost makes leaves loud, so walk in on bare trail dirt and move only after the sun melts the frost. Every shot goes between NW and N, with trunks and ground behind.

steps.text: Leave the yard by the main trail. Red light only. Walk on bare dirt, not frosted leaves. 20 steps, stop 10 seconds. Gun unloaded.
Turn onto the loop trail and climb to the center rise. Step 15 yards off the trail to the pine. Sit facing NW. Load #4, plug in. Red light off.
Legal light. Do not move. Scan the trunks 20 to 40 yards out, from W round to N. Squirrels stay in the nest in frost.
Sunrise. Watch for the first sunlit trunks. Do the shot-placement check (see skill) on each one you scan, but do not shoot yet.
Sun reaches the feed trees. Peak squirrel time begins. Use the leaf-scratch call once, then stay still for 10 minutes.
Frost is gone and the leaves are damp and quiet. Still-hunt slowly north to the swamp edge, into the wind. 3 steps, 20 seconds still. Shots N only.
Walk the swamp edge to the Junction. Check the mud for snipe and tracks. Crow check: listen for calls overhead.
Loop to the feed bins. Walk the sunny edge of the thick cover for rabbit. Shoot N or W only; never toward the field SE.
Unload at the bins. Walk out by the main trail. Do the land task on the way.

items: **In the gun: #4** (plug in, 3 shells max). Good for squirrel to 35 yards.
**Right pocket: #7.5** for dove, crow, snipe, or a close rabbit.
**Slugs: zipped in a separate pocket.** Bear defense only.
**No 00 buckshot today.** It stays home.
**Choke: Modified.**
**.22 LR (optional):** head shots on still squirrels only, with a trunk or the ground behind the squirrel.
Pack - GRAB: gun, phone, water bottle filled, tell someone your plan and return time.
Pack - CHARGE: headlamp and spare flashlight before bed.
Pack - RESTOCK after the hunt: water, coffee or tea, nibble, nitrile gloves, .22 LR count, fatwood.
warnings: Never shoot a deer with birdshot. Not with #4, not with #7.5.
Swap shells in the open with the muzzle north. Count every shell in and out.
Cold hands are slow hands. Keep your finger outside the guard until the shot is sure.

animals.name: Gray squirrel and fox squirrel
paragraphs: The most common game on the property. Grays work the hardwoods, holly, and swamp edge. A fox squirrel, bigger and orange-brown, may show in the open pines.
In frost they wait in the nest until the sun finds the trunks, then feed hard for an hour or two. Expect the best window from 7:15 to 9:00.

details.title: Shot and load
steps: #4 at 20 to 35 yards. Aim at the head and neck of a squirrel on a trunk.
With the .22: head only, with wood or ground behind the squirrel.
After the shot, wait 10 minutes. Others freeze, then move again.
details.note: Mark the fall against a trunk or stump before you move.

details.title: Call: leaf scratch
steps: Reach down and rake dry leaves with your fingers.
Make 3 or 4 short scratches, pause 2 seconds, then 3 or 4 more.
Stop for 10 minutes. Watch for a head or tail flick.
It sounds like a squirrel digging a nut. Use it from the seat only, after the frost is off.

after: Tip: a bright tail edge lit by the low sun gives away a squirrel that the bark hides.
Tip: a squirrel that circles the trunk away from you will come back around if you stay still for 2 minutes.

animals.name: Rabbit
paragraphs: Cottontails use the thick edges near the feed bins and the pine-holly thickets.
After a frosty night they sit at the first warm edge of cover once the sun hits it, and they trust their color.

details.title: Shot and load
steps: #4 or #7.5 at 15 to 25 yards. Aim at the head and front shoulders.
Shoot only with the ground behind the rabbit.
Never shoot toward the south line or the field SE.

details.title: Technique: edge walk
steps: Walk the sunny edge of a thicket slowly, into the wind.
Look for the round black eye and the ear line, not the whole body.
Stop 15 yards short. Wait 30 seconds. A rabbit that thinks it is seen will run.

after: Tip: wear gloves to clean rabbits. Discard any rabbit with white spots on the liver.

animals.name: Raccoon and opossum
paragraphs: Both feed at night along the swamp and around the feed bins. At first light the last ones head for hollow trees and root dens. Frost shows fresh tracks well.

details.title: Shot and load
steps: #4 to the head at 20 yards or less.
Approach from behind. Touch the eye with a stick to confirm it is dead. Opossums play dead.
details.note: Wear gloves. Rabies is possible in raccoons.

after: Tip: dark tracks on pale frost are fresh. A track with frost inside it is old.

animals.name: Crow
paragraphs: Crows roost off the property and fly over to feed. Saturday is a legal day. On clear cold mornings they fly early and steady.

details.title: Shot and load
steps: #7.5 at 35 yards or less. Swing through the bird and keep the gun moving.
Shoot north only, with no house or field beyond the bird.

details.title: Technique: stay hidden
steps: Sit in shade with your back to the pine. Keep your face down.
Look up with your eyes, not your head.
Shoot the first bird that sets its wings and drops.

after: Tip: crows mobbing in the trees mean they found an owl or a hawk. Walk quietly toward the noise.

animals.name: Mourning dove
paragraphs: Doves pass between the pasture and the swamp pines in the first hour of light. Segment 2 runs Nov 7 to 28. Shooting hours start at legal light. HIP certification and a 3-shell plug are required.

details.title: Shot and load
steps: #7.5 at 25 to 35 yards. Swing through the bird, then fire without stopping the gun.
Shoot only north, high enough that the shot clears the trees. Never toward the field SE.

after: Tip: a dove shot over the swamp falls in water or mud. Mark it before you shoot.

animals.name: Snipe
paragraphs: Snipe feed in the wet mud and shallows at the swamp edge. They flush with a harsh scaipe call and zig-zag. HIP certification and a 3-shell plug are required.

details.title: Technique: let it straighten
steps: Walk the mud margin slowly into the wind.
When a snipe flushes, wait. It zig-zags for 10 to 15 yards, then flies straight.
Shoot #7.5 once it levels out, north only.

after: Tip: look for small round probe holes in soft mud.

animals.name: Bear and bobcat
paragraphs: Awareness only. Bear season opens today, so you may hear other hunters. Give a bear space, talk out loud, and back away. Slugs are for defense only.

skill.title: Shot placement and backstops: #4, #7.5, and .22 LR
skill.principle: A clean shot is placement plus backstop. Know where the pellets or bullet go, and what they hit if you miss. If the backstop is not certain, do not shoot.

sections.title: Squirrel with #4 or #7.5
steps: Aim at the head and neck. Pellets in the head kill fast and leave the meat clean.
A squirrel on a trunk: aim at the head, with the trunk behind it. Pellets that miss hit wood.
A squirrel on a limb in the open: only shoot if the sky is north of you and nothing stands beyond. Shot can carry 100 yards or more.
Keep range at 20 to 35 yards. Closer is cleaner. Farther cripples.

sections.title: Squirrel with the .22 LR
steps: Head shot only. A body shot ruins meat and can wound.
The squirrel must have a big trunk or the ground behind it. A .22 bullet can travel over a mile.
Never shoot at a squirrel against the sky or against thin branches.
If the squirrel moves, wait. Do not follow it with the muzzle through anything you would not shoot.

sections.title: The 4-second backstop check
steps: Look past the animal: what stops a miss?
Look left and right: is the whole arc inside NW to N?
Look at the ground: is the slope toward you or away?
Say it quietly: trunk, ground, north, clear. Then shoot.

sections.title: After the shot
steps: Keep the gun pointed north and stay seated for a slow count of 10.
Mark the fall against a trunk, stump, or fork.
Walk to it with the gun unloaded if you must cross open ground.

details.title: Why it matters in the frost
paragraphs: Cold fingers and heavy gloves rush shots. Take your time: a squirrel in sunlight stays for a minute. Waiting for a trunk behind it costs nothing.

skill.checkpoint: Before your first shot, say the backstop check out loud in your head. After the hunt, send a note: about which shots you passed because the backstop was wrong.

land.intro: You learn the land by reading what the squirrels leave behind.
steps: On the walk out, pick the 2 best feed trees you passed: biggest pile of fresh cuttings.
Pace each from the Junction and note the tree type if you know it.
Look at where the frost melted first. Those sunny spots are where squirrels and rabbits will sit.
Send what you find with a note: message, for example: note: feed trees, 2 oaks, 40 and 70 paces from Junction, sun hit the rise at 7:10.

safety: NEVER shoot south. The house is SW and the field is SE: no-shoot directions.
Every shot today goes between NW and N, with the ground or a trunk behind the animal.
Hunter orange hat and vest are required (Oct 17 to Jan 1). Deer gun season is still open for other hunters, and bear opens today.
Sky shots (dove, crow) only to the north, above the treeline.
Frost makes trails and logs slick. Unload before crossing logs or the swamp edge.
It is about 34F at walk-in. Wear layers you can open as it warms.

hunts.gaps: No hour-by-hour forecast was available for the hunt morning, so no hourly chart is shown, and no gust or rain chance was listed. The forecast was updated Friday afternoon. The point used may not match the property exactly. Sunrise and legal light (sunrise minus 30 minutes) were carried from an earlier calculation because the sun table could not be fetched tonight. The moon figures come from a monthly table. Migratory dates (dove, snipe, rails, ducks, woodcock, crow) and quail were checked earlier this week and not re-checked tonight. Bag limits for squirrel, rabbit, raccoon, opossum, quail, and crow were not found.
